report.summary: Literature does not give a single definitive number. Mutation testing work (e.g., Inozemtseva & Holmes, 2014) suggests 20–50 mutants can approximate full mutant set metrics, but this is for mutation score, not defect-detector thresholds. Studies on synthetic defect injection for prediction (e.g., Just et al., 2014) show mutants can mimic real faults incompletely; thresholds from mutants diverge from real-defect thresholds by an uncertain margin. Recommendation: per-project empirical convergence analysis with bootstrapping; start with ≥200 mutants, validate with historical defects if available.
risks: Mutant-based thresholds may overfit to artificial patterns, causing missed critical defects (fail-open risk) or excessive false positives.
Without real-defect data, calibration uncertainty persists; synthetic-to-real transfer gap is unquantified broadly.
todos: Implement bootstrapping on synthetic corpus to determine threshold stability point (likely 100–500 mutants).
Collect a small set of real post-mortem defects (≥20) for validation and potential threshold adjustment.
Start with a conservative threshold (e.g., top 5% of mutant suspiciousness scores) and monitor in production.

handoff.suggestion: Review recent literature on 'synthetic defect injection for prediction calibration' (e.g., TSE 2021 studies). Consider using a holdout set of real defects to adjust thresholds if project history allows.

name: q37-cold-start-thresholds
question: When calibrating a defect detector per project using synthetic corpora, how many synthetic examples are needed before thresholds stabilise, and how much does a threshold calibrated on synthetic mutants differ from one calibrated on real defects?
